newsitem.title: USA: Actor Lew Ayres dies at age 88.
newsitem.headline: Actor Lew Ayres dies at age 88.

text.p: Actor Lew Ayres, whose career spanned seven decades during which he appeared in more than 60 films, has died at the age of 88.

Ayres, who was the original Dr. Kildare, may be best remembered for his role as a disillusioned German soldier in the 1930 classic "All Quiet on the Western Front" and for his real-life conflict with the military.

Hollywood studios and moviegoers across America shunned him when he declared himself a conscientious objector and refused to fight in World War Two. Eventually, he volunteered to serve as a medic and chaplain's aide, earning three battle stars, and his show business career was restored.
The William Morris Agency said Ayres died in his sleep at his Los Angeles home early on Monday. He is survived by his widow, Diana and his son Justin.
Ayres' first major film was 1929's "The Kiss" with Greta Garbo, followed by "All Quiet on the Western Front," an anti-war film in which he played a young German soldier fighting in World War One.
In 1938, movie mogul Louis B. Mayer chose him for the lead role in "Young Dr. Kildare." It was to be the first of nine successful films featuring Ayres as the crusading young physician.

He lost favour with Hollywood and the public when he announced after being drafted into the military in 1942 that he would not fight. "In my opinion we will never stop wars until we individually cease fighting them, and that is what I propose to do," Ayres said in a statement at the time.

But it was his strong religious beliefs, and not his fear of fighting, that prompted his actions, and he went on to become a hero, tending to the wounded on the battle lines in the Philippines and New Guinea.

After the war Ayres was welcomed back by Hollywood and made several critically acclaimed films, including "The Dark Mirror" (1946), "The Unfaithful" (1947) and "Johnny Belinda" (1948), in which he played a kindly, small-town doctor.
He was nominated for a best actor Oscar for "Johnny Belinda" but did not win. His co-star, Jane Wyman, won the best actress award for her role as a deaf-mute rape victim.

In the 1960s Ayres appeared in such movies as "Advise and Consent" and "The Carpetbaggers," and in the 1970s was featured in "Battle for the Planet of the Apes," "Damien - Omen II" and "Battlestar Galactica."
His television credits included "Hawaii Five-O," "Francis Gary Powers," "Salem's Lot," "Of Mice and Men" and "Lime Street."
Ayres was married three times, in 1931 to actress Lola Lane, in 1934 to film star Ginger Rogers, and in 1965 to Diana Hall, who was a flight attendant at the time of their marriage.
